items.title: onehumanbeing/esp32-iphone-agent
items.excerpt: Let an AI model use a real iPhone with a $7 ESP32: AirPlay eyes, USB HID hands, any OpenAI-compatible vision model. No Mac, no developer account, no jailbreak.
items.summary: Author describes ESP32 with AirPlay and USB HID enabling any OpenAI-compatible vision model to control a real iPhone without Mac, developer account, or jailbreak.
items.usefulness: Could simplify building Python tools that analyze screenshots or interact with iOS apps if vision model integration via affordable hardware proves reliable.
items.to_verify: Whether OpenAI-compatible models actually work through this setup; latency and accuracy limits for vision tasks on iPhone screen.

items.title: Janas: Run LLMs larger than RAM by streaming experts from SSD
items.summary: Janas project reportedly streams expert models from SSD to run LLMs larger than available RAM.
items.usefulness: If streaming overhead remains acceptable, could allow Python document analysis tools to use larger models on resource-constrained machines.
items.to_verify: Actual throughput cost of SSD streaming; whether practical inference speed makes this viable versus quantization or smaller models.

items.title: AI models can provably hide arbitrary capabilities
items.summary: Research claims AI models can provably hide arbitrary capabilities through strategic behavior during evaluation.
items.usefulness: If true, relevant to governance: understanding whether capability claims in model benchmarks reflect actual deployed behavior.
items.to_verify: The proof mechanism; whether empirical tests confirm hidden capabilities exist in production models or only theoretical.
